payload.quote: Here we quantitatively review over a decade of research, showing that choice architecture interventions successfully promote behavior change across key behavioral domains, populations, and locations.
payload.test: Refuted if mhhb_nma_analysis.R, run on mhhb_nma_data_corrected.csv, fits primary_robust or domain_robust on k ≠ 447, or if primary_robust's intercept, any of domain_robust's six domain coefficients (not scale(year)) or their 95% CI limits, rounded half away from zero to two decimals, differs from corrected Table 2: overall 0.43 [0.38, 0.48]; health 0.34 [0.25, 0.43], food 0.65 [0.47, 0.83], environment 0.43 [0.33, 0.54], finance 0.24 [0.14, 0.35], pro-social 0.41 [0.27, 0.54], other 0.31 [0.09, 0.52]. Inconclusive if the run stops or times out, or gives no finite value for a compared figure.

scope.basis: Publication years of the included records, corrected Table 2 (PNAS 119(19), e2204059119): "Year of publication 1982 to 2021". Methods: "The search concluded in June 2019". The corrected abstract says 440 effect sizes; Table 2 and the posted data have 447, used here.

fidelity.basis: The paper's own script and corrected data; ours is the rule: its printed figures must be reproduced. A computational check, its targets known in advance, testing no new sample; it does not address the publication-bias objections (Maier et al. 2022, doi:10.1073/pnas.2200300119), nor populations and locations, which the paper tests only as moderators.
